prior.reason: No source describes the Northwest Ridge. The search found Dry Creek reports, SummitPost (403) noting that the north-side routes start from the Ice Caves viewpoint, and a 1974 AAJ note on a North Face gully (13 h round trip). None of these covers this route.
The Tower Route (on the NE ridge) appears only in passing in CascadeClimbers threads (403) and a SummitPost access note (403). No opened source gives its length, timing or descent.
The only description is a one-line SummitPost note ('ascend from Hester Lake trail; route finding and bushwhack'), seen as a search snippet; the page returns 403. No trip report covers this line.

The East Buttress is described only on SummitPost (Wing Lake start, gully system, class 3-4, 'long strenuous day or comfortable weekend'), seen as a search snippet; the page returns 403. No second source covers the route.
Only first-ascent history (June 1971) turned up. The Yellowleaf Burnt Boot page lists one 2012 trip that came from the Iceberg Lake side; none covers the north ridge or the Middle Fork ford.

No new sources this run. The written-up approach crosses the border on foot from Manning Park, which is not lawful, and nothing found covers the lawful Harts Pass/PCT approach the row names (roughly 30 mi each way).
Only first-ascent material exists, and that party approached from Canada. Nothing found gives camps or timing for the lawful Ross Lake / Freezeout Creek approach to the north face.

The only route description is an OpenBeta entry seen as a search snippet (5.7, a long ridge 0.65 mi summit to summit, double ropes advised); the page 404'd on fetch. The other results were ski circumnavigations, so there is no sourced timing or day structure.
No source describes the East Face (the row's descent is 'presumed'). Northern Pickets approach material covers other routes, and CascadeClimbers/SummitPost return 403. No new searches were possible.

The only opened source is the 1988 AAJ note (IV 5.10, about 4,000 ft, 'a difficult approach' to the northern cirque, topped out under a full moon). It gives no approach route, camps or descent. A second source (ademiller) 404'd and SummitPost returns 403.

Two opened FA reports (AAJ 2009 and Alpinist 2008) describe this route: two days of bushwhacking via the McMillan Creek glacier remnants to a Sourdough Ridge camp, about 3.5 h to the base, then 7 + 7 + 11 pitches over three days with two bivies and a same-day rappel. But neither gives mileage, gain, camp elevations or approach/walk-out hours, so the approach and exit days would have no sourced figure. The reports also disagree on length (AAJ says 29 pitches, Alpinist 25 pitches / ~2,400 ft). Sources: http://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/12200911000/North-America-United-States-Washington-East-McMillan-Spire-Come-Over-to-the-Dark-Side, https://alpinist.com/doc/web08f/newswire-kearney-east-mcmillan

Opened sources (wenatcheeoutdoors 2016, hike2hike 2023) describe the Trinity / Chiwawa River approach to the 6,300 ft bench and the Fortress East Ridge and gully routes (about 20 mi and 7,900 ft with Chiwawa), but neither mentions the Northeast Face, so the summit day can't be described.

Opened North Peak reports use other lines: drdirtbag (2017) did a one-day, ~12 h ascent from Hozomeen Lake via the SW peak and the connecting ridge to the Class 3 southeast face, and mountainflamingo (2018) climbed the north ridge from Canada over two days. stevensong's page truncated before the report. None describes the North Peak's south ridge.

The only opened source touching the northeast shoulder (climberkyle 2021) is a 22-mile, 13.5 h single-day Big Snow-Iron Cap traverse that descended the northeast side. No opened source describes an ascent from Tank Lakes / Foss River with camps or per-day figures; earlier local research cites only a peakbagger snippet (403) for the NE shoulder.

No opened source climbs Crowder. trailcatjim's Picket traverse from Perfect Pass skips it, and the only earlier mention (Abegg) came from the south. There is no camp, day or timing beta for the Easy Ridge / Perfect Pass approach to the Phantom-Crowder col.

Two opened Mount Lincoln reports (explorerron 2024, one attempt and one ascent) climb from Upper Staircase directly up the southern Sawtooth ridge in a day, about 10 mi and 12+ h, via an unnamed chockstone chute. Neither names or describes the Harniss Chute or the Flapjack Lakes approach in the row.
